note:
External reference geometry for blind benchmarks. Nothing here is committed: these are third-party artifacts, and AGENTS.md forbids putting them in this repository. ARCHITECTURE.md 16.6 is the rule they follow instead -- a corpus that stays external and is referenced by stable identity and hash. `tools/corpus.py` fetches them and verifies every digest.

NOTHING HERE MAY DESCRIBE THE GEOMETRY. An entry names what a part is *for*, never what it measures. The first version of this file carried each reference's bounding box in its `note` , correct to the stated precision, which is the answer a blind benchmark exists to withhold, committed in plaintext beside the id, in the file a request generator would read. Found by review. `tools/test_corpus.py` now refuses a note that contains a dimension, because a wall kept by remembering is not a wall.

voron2.why: Real functional printed parts designed around standard hardware -- M3 fasteners, 2020 extrusion, MGN rails, GT2 belts. That matters for a blind benchmark: the request can state what the part has to interface with, in the vocabulary a person would actually use, without stating any geometry. The dimensions are the answer and are never in the request.

entries.note: Supports a deck panel against extrusion. Single body, watertight.
Holds an MGN9 rail true to an extrusion while it is bolted down. Single body, watertight.
Retains a bottom panel in the extrusion slot. Single body, watertight.
Clamps a GT2 belt end. Single body, watertight.
